pointers.sentence: The four views are in `django.contrib.auth.urls`: `"password_reset/"` asks for the address, `"password_reset/done/"` says a mail went out, `"reset/<uidb64>/<token>/"` is the link, and `"reset/done/"` says the password was set (`django/contrib/auth/urls.py`).

When the form is valid it calls `PasswordResetForm.save` with the view's templates and token generator, the request, and `use_https=self.request.is_secure()`, then redirects to `"password_reset_done"` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordResetView`).

It asks the default manager for the active users whose email field (`AbstractBaseUser.get_email_field_name`) matches by `"__iexact"`; then, in Python, it keeps those with a usable password whose stored address equals the typed one under `_unicode_ci_compare`: NFKC normalization and case folding, the comparison Unicode Technical Report 36 recommends, as its docstring says (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.get_users`, `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:_unicode_ci_compare`).

The visitor is told the same either way: the view redirects to the done page whether a mail was sent or not, which the documentation says keeps an attacker from learning which addresses exist; it warns that the time a mail takes to send may tell it all the same (`docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).
Nor does a failed send show: it is caught and logged to `"django.contrib.auth"` (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.send_mail`).

For each user, `save` makes the context of the mail's templates: `"uid"`, the primary key as a string in URL-safe base64 by `urlsafe_base64_encode` ([The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md)); `"token"`, from `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.make_token`; `"protocol"`, `"https"` or `"http"`; `"domain"` and `"site_name"`, from `get_current_site` unless a caller gives `save` a domain_override, as the view does not; without `django.contrib.sites` that is a `RequestSite` whose name and domain are both the request's host; `"user"` and `"email"`; and the view's `extra_email_context` over them all (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.save`, `django/contrib/sites/shortcuts.py:get_current_site`).

`PasswordResetForm.send_mail` renders the subject and joins its lines into one, since, its comment says, a subject must not contain newlines; it renders the body and sends an `EmailMultiAlternatives`, with an HTML alternative only when the view names an HTML template ([Email messages: `EmailMessage` and `EmailMultiAlternatives`](../services/email-messages.md), [Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.send_mail`).

`PasswordResetTokenGenerator.make_token` passes to `PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_token_with_timestamp` the seconds from the start of 2001 to now, read as local time with no zone, and the generator's secret (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now`).

The second is `salted_hmac` of `PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value`, salted with `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.key_salt`, the class's dotted path, with `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.algorithm`, SHA-256 unless a subclass names another, keeping every second hex digit, 32 of 64, to shorten the URL, as the comment says (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_token_with_timestamp`).

`default_token_generator` is the module's one instance, the default of the views and of `save` (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:default_token_generator`).

`_make_hash_value` joins as text the user's primary key, the stored password string, the last login with its microseconds and zone dropped, or nothing before the first login, the timestamp, and the user's email, or nothing (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value`).
Last, it refuses a timestamp more than `PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT` seconds old, 259,200 (three days) by default (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`).
The documentation says a shorter timeout makes a token no harder to guess, since tokens are designed to be safe from brute force without one (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).

It finds the user with `PasswordResetConfirmView.get_user`, which decodes the base64, converts it with the primary key field's `to_python`, and asks the default manager; a value that does not decode, convert or name a user gives no user, and the page for an invalid link (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordResetConfirmView.get_user`).
With a user there are two cases (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordResetConfirmView.dispatch`):

`PasswordResetConfirmView.form_valid` saves it, which sets the password and saves the user; deletes the session's entry; logs the user in, with `PasswordResetConfirmView.post_reset_login_backend`, only if `PasswordResetConfirmView.post_reset_login` is true, which by default it is not; and redirects to `PasswordResetCompleteView` (`django/contrib/auth/views.py:PasswordResetConfirmView.form_valid`).
